data.long_meaning: In Hebrew mythology, Alphiel is an angelic being whose name is derived from El, the Hebrew word for 'God'. In Christian tradition, the name Alphiel is not directly associated with any specific biblical character or saint. The name Alphiel carries the meaning “El, God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Alphiel usually hope their child will grow to embody el, god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine wisdom, power, and protection.
data.etymology: Alphiel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “El, God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alphiel total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: אלפיאל
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא מלך שלי, אלוהים משחרר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלפיאל הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא מלך שלי' או 'אלוהים משחרר'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'אלף' שמשמעותו אלוהים או אל, ו'אל' שמשמעותו מלך או משחרר. השם אלפיאל מופיע בתנ"ך כבן של אליעזר, בן של משה (שמות יח 4, במדבר ג 29). השם נושא משמעות רבה בהקשר של היחסים בין אלוהים לאדם, והוא משקף את התפיסה היהודית של אלוהים כמלך וכמשחרר.

in_greek.name: Αλφιήλ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι ο βασιλιάς μου, ο Θεός ελευθερώνει
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αλφιήλ είναι ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος אלפיאל, που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι ο βασιλιάς μου' ή 'ο Θεός ελευθερώνει'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα, αλλά η ετυμολογία του σχετίζεται με την έννοια του Θεού ως βασιλιά και ελευθερωτή. Το όνομα Αλφιήλ χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία και αντανακλά την πίστη των πρώτων Χριστιανών στην κυριαρχία και τη σωτηρία του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Alphiel
in_latin.meaning: Deus est rex meus, Deus liberat
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Alphiel derivatur ex hebraeo nomine אלפיאל, quod significat 'Deus est rex meus' vel 'Deus liberat'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Alphiel usitatum erat et reflectebat fidem Christianorum in dominio et salvatione Dei. Etymologia nominis Alphiel connectitur cum conceptu Dei ut rex et liberator, quod est fundamentum theologiae christianae.

in_english.name: Alphiel
in_english.meaning: God is my king, God releases or liberates
in_english.long_meaning: The name Alphiel originates from the Hebrew name אלפיאל (Alphiel), meaning 'God is my king' or 'God releases'. It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'El' (אל), meaning God, and 'Phiel' (אל), meaning king or releases. Alphiel appears in the Bible as a son of Eleazar, a son of Moses (Exodus 18:4, Numbers 3:29). The name carries significant spiritual meaning in the context of God's relationship with humanity, reflecting the Jewish and Christian concept of God as king and liberator. Historically, the name has been used in Christian tradition to signify faith in God's sovereignty and redemption.

data.cultural_impact: The name Alphiel holds no significant cultural impact in popular culture or in the Judeo-Christian tradition as it is not associated with any well-known mythological, legendary, or historical figure. Its association with Hebrew mythology and Christian tradition is largely academic or scholarly in nature.
data.spiritual_significance: Alphiel is a name with deep spiritual roots as it is derived from El, the Hebrew word for 'God'. It is often used in spiritual and metaphysical contexts as a reminder of the divine origin and nature of all beings. The name Alphiel invites us to consider our connection to the divine, to remember that we are all part of the divine tapestry, and to strive towards spiritual growth and enlightenment. It is a powerful reminder of the unity and interconnectedness of all things, and of the ultimate power and presence of the divine in our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Alphiel is believed to be an angel or a good fairy in Hebrew folklore. She is described as a healer and a protector of children, symbolizing love, compassion, and nurturing. Her name may be derived from the Hebrew words "El" (God) and "Phiel" (loving kindness).

biblical_reference.note: Son of Eleazar, son of Moses

historical_references.reference: Alphiel is mentioned in the pseudo-epigrapha 'The Book of Jubilees', which is a Jewish work written around the 2nd century BC that interprets and expands biblical history. Alphiel is described as the chief of the fallen angels, the 'Watchers', who came to Earth to cohabit with human women and produce the Nephilim giants.

In Christian legend, Alphiel is one of the most beautiful and powerful of the succubi, or female demonic entities believed to visit men in their dreams and tempt them with carnal desire. This association is most likely derived from her earlier identity as a fallen angel and the association of fallen angels with sexual temptation.

modern_usage.modern_context: Alphiel is a folklore figure from Christian mythology, traditionally known as a succubus. However, in contemporary culture, she is often reimagined as a neutral or even benevolent figure. Alphiel has gained popularity in various modern contexts, particularly in Wicca and Paganism as a goddess, and in role-playing games, including D&D 5th Edition and other Tabletop RPGs, where players can create characters based on her or invoke her name for various purposes.
